messages:
Acme Sandra: Hey team, seeing intermittent 504s from the hosted inference endpoint during our peak batch jobs this morning. Happens ~10% of requests when concurrency > 120. sample request-id: req_xxx_9f2a

maya.patel: sorry to hear that — can you paste a curl/SDK snippet and the exact timestamps so we can correlate logs? :wave:

Acme Sandra: here's a minimal curl we used (we're on sdk-js 2.4.1):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_xxx_9f2a" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b", "input":"...", "max_tokens":256}'
```

Acme Sandra: Timestamp window: 2026-03-14T09:12:21Z -> 09:19:05Z, about 300 calls/minute. SDK client showed repeated 504s and then retried immediately (no backoff configured).

samir.khan: thanks — initial hypothesis: gateway timeouts due to backend pod queueing + aggressive client retries. Can you confirm if you disabled client-side exponential backoff?

Acme Sandra: yes, currently retry config is default, which retried 3x with no jitter. Changing that is a pain for us right now (we need a short-term workaround).

lena.ortiz: @samir.khan I'll pull gateway traces for those req ids. @maya.patel can you check if there were any model rollouts or autoscale events during that window?

maya.patel: no rollouts. I see a scale-up attempt at 09:15 but pods stayed at target; however the gateway's p95 queue time spiked to ~700ms. Also seeing some 502s from the proxy layer: `upstream prematurely closed connection` around same window.

igor.novak: adding that we have a known issue where under heavy small-request bursts the connection pool can exhaust and cause 502/504 cascades. Ops has a mitigation patch but it's staged.

samir.khan: can we get repro steps so eng can reproduce in a harness? Lazy approach: hammer with 150 concurrent curl processes for 2 min with no backoff + keepalive disabled. More faithful: use the customer's SDK config and concurrency.

Acme Sandra: putting together a tiny repro script now. Will share later in thread. Prefer to avoid full blast against prod — can we try a canary route?

maya.patel: we can cut a temporary canary route to a separate pool, and enable a higher per-connection timeout for them. Two options: (1) increase gateway timeout from 60s->120s for the route; (2) enable temporary circuit-breaker with fast-fail after 2s queueing. Which do you prefer?

Acme Sandra: +1 for option (1) if it reduces errors while we fix retries client-side. Option (2) might fail more requests, which worries product.

igor.novak: ops note: increasing gateway timeout helps for long requests but masks backend saturation — it may increase latency but reduce 504s. Also turning on connection pool growth for that pool is doable. I'll trigger a pool-size bump for the canary.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created: DPL-4521 by igor.novak — increase gateway timeout for route customer-acme to 120s and bump pool_size=50 -> 100. ETA ~10m.

maya.patel: created ticket SUP-7892 to track. Linking logs + traces: https://internal.logs/redwood/requests?rid=req_xxx_9f2a (redacted). Key trace error from gateway: `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection` then `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)`.

samir.khan: for repro, here's a small script we use in-house to simulate behavior (will post to the customer's shared bucket):

```
#!/bin/bash
# simulate bursty clients
for i in $(seq 1 150); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "X-Request-ID: repro_$i" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```

lena.ortiz: test run on staging with sdk-js 2.4.1 reproduced increased 504s when no jitter/backoff and concurrency>120. We also saw `rpc: connection closed` from backend A.

Acme Sandra: thanks, if you can run that in a canary pool and confirm reduction before we change prod, that'd be great.

igor.novak: running canary now. Temporary mitigation result: after bumping pool_size and timeout, customer route error rate down from 9.8%->1.2% over 15m. Still seeing some 502s during spikes but much improved.

maya.patel: rolling the canary config into customer's prod route. Notifying customer.

Acme Sandra: confirmed — error rate reduced on our side. One follow-up: can you provide recommended client-side retry/backoff settings?

samir.khan: recommended minimal config for sdk-js: exponential backoff with jitter, base_delay=200ms, max_delay=5s, max_retries=2. Also enable connection pooling and keepalive. Example snippet:

```
// pseudo-config
client.configure({
  retries: 2,
  backoff: { base: 200, cap: 5000, jitter: true }
});
```

lena.ortiz: open action items: SUP-7892 (prod mitigation), ENG-3245 (root cause: pool exhaustion + gateway queueing; long-term fix), DOCS-192 (add retry guidance in SDK docs). I'll assign ENG-3245 to @igor.novak and ENG-3245 PR will include a load test.

igor.novak: I'll also add a transient metric alert for gateway queue time > 500ms to catch earlier.

deploy-bot: Deploy DPL-4521 succeeded.

Acme Sandra: Thanks everyone — reduced errors and clear next steps. We'll implement client backoff this week. :white_check_mark:

maya.patel: marking this thread as resolved but keeping SUP-7892 open until client changes are verified. If anything regresses ping @oncall. :rotating_light:

samir.khan: quick note for postmortem: capture sampling of `X-Request-ID` mapping to backend pod to verify if a small set of pods were saturated. We saw hints of KV-cache misses under burst load causing longer tails.

Acme Sandra: appreciated. Will re-open if we see flares after SDK changes. Thanks all!
